label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
On Saturday, we wrapped up the student-run Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms, held from 5–7 November 2026 in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune.

Writing on behalf of my fellow organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, and myself: thank you to everyone who made these three days possible.

We welcomed 41 MSc and early PhD participants from 9 states, selected from 112 applications on the basis of a statement and one reference. Our institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh supported the school, covering hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) for the lectures on Mordell–Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) for modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, joining online from Kraków, for computations in Sage. We are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance.

Two moments will stay with me. When the power went out for nearly two hours on the second afternoon and our laptops ran out of charge, we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be my favourite session of the school.

An MSc student from Silchar also spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer’s notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. That exchange captured something I hope we can keep: students feeling able to question what is on the board.

A special thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm after a booking mix-up, and to all the office staff and volunteers. Our six PhD teaching assistants made the problem sessions work; this is a format we want to retain.

Thank you, above all, to the participants for their questions and persistence. For MSc students, I think small schools like this can offer something harder to find at a large conference: time to ask questions, try things out, and learn alongside others.

Slides and problem sheets will be posted on the department website within two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to grant funding. We would love to build on what worked this time.
